record.title: Bhutan-facing gates close for West Bengal’s April 2026 first-phase election
record.scope: Ordinary entry/exit at three Bhutan–India gates
record.movement: Ordinary cross-border users; no universal all-goods claim.
record.exceptions: NDTV’s Jaigaon account exempts tourists and essential services. Applicability of those exceptions at the other two gates is not established.
record.imposing_authority: Bhutan Ministry of Home Affairs / district administration; Indian authorities at Jaigaon also reported closure
record.enforcement: Original Bhutanese order covers three gates; separate Indian-side reporting supports physical Jaigaon closure.
record.relationship: Separate West Bengal first-phase measure from Tamulpur April 6–9 (R5-SC-003) and Benapole April 26–30 (R3-SC-001). Counterpart action is grouped, not counted as two national shutdowns.
record.status_observation: Official three-gate order; Jaigaon closure reported April 20. April 23 at 18:00 is scheduled reopening, not observed resumption.
record.official_rationale: West Bengal Legislative Assembly elections; Indian account cites prevention of unwanted activity.
record.context: Reciprocal frontier measure preceding April 23 voting.
record.uncertainty: Official notice gives 17:00 while Jaigaon reporting says after 18:00; no harmonized hour assumed. Other gates have order-level evidence only. No observed April 23 reopening.

historical.duration_note: Scheduled or ordered reopening; actual operational duration not established. No measured continuous interval is established.
